title: Isoniazid
dek: A hydrazide prodrug, KatG-activated, InhA-blocked, rapidly cidal against replicating bacilli. NAT2 slow acetylators, pyridoxine, and hepatotoxicity are the host half of the plate.
story: Isoniazid (isonicotinic acid hydrazide) is small, cheap, and still the early-cidal pillar of DS-TB and of most TPT. KatG activates it; INH–NAD inhibits InhA; mycolate synthesis collapses in replicating cells. It is a weak sterilizing drug in caseum. That is why six months of INH can be TPT and why INH monotherapy of cavitary disease is how katG mutants are born in public.

Host NAT2 acetylates INH. Slow acetylators have higher AUC and more hepatitis/neuropathy risk; fast acetylators may have lower levels. Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) prevents INH neuropathy, especially in pregnancy, HIV, malnutrition, and diabetes. Hepatotoxicity is shared with PZA and RIF — stop the right drug, not the whole alphabet by panic.
WHO adult dose 5 mg/kg (cap 300 mg); children ~10 mg/kg bands. High-dose INH (10–15 mg/kg) appears in some Hr/MDR recipes only for low-level inhA alleles. S315T does not care.
deep: PubChem CID 3767; ChEMBL64. Not a rifamycin, not a hydrazine street drug — a hydrazide antibiotic.
ahpC promoter-up often compensates katG loss. Do not treat ahpC as the primary INH call.
Cross-R with ETH is an inhA story. Cross-R with PAS is not.
CDC overlay matches WHO on INH as TPT and DS backbone; NAT2 genotyping is research-ish in most programmes.

visual.caption: INH from tablet to InhA, with the host NAT2 off-ramp and the pyridoxine patch for neuropathy.

example.title: 60 kg adult, neuropathy, no B6
example.setup: Week 8 of HRZE, burning feet, ALT normal, HIV-negative, no pyridoxine prescribed.

steps.title: This is INH neuropathy until proven otherwise
steps.body: Start B6, examine for other neuropathies (diabetes, LZD if they were on it — they were not).

steps.title: Dose was 300 mg
steps.body: 5 mg/kg × 60, capped. Still enough for neuropathy without B6.

steps.title: Do not stop RIF for neuropathy
steps.body: Wrong toxicity. Stopping the sterilizing drug for an INH nerve is a classic error.

example.takeaway: INH: cidal, prodrug, B6, not the sterilizing star.
